To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the shape of the proton momentum spectrum is determined by the momentum distribution of nucleons in the projectile and by the degree of excita-tion of the fragmenting system.
the shape of the spectrum of protons from 16Op at a momentum of about 3 GeV/c per proton depends on the degree of excitaion of the projectile nucleus.

the degree of the excitation of the nucleus in 16Op collision affects predominantly the shape (the slope of the spectra) of the momentum spectra of protons in the backward hemisphere and partly the shape (the position of the maximum) of the spectra of the forward hemisphere protons formed via the mechanisms Fermi breakup and emission.

the momentum features of proton fragments emitted from collisions of 16Op projectiles with a carbon target at a projectile momentum of 3 GeV/c per projectile nucleon.
the momentum features of proton emission from excited nuclei formed in 16Op interactions at 3.25 AGeV.
the analysis of the momentum spectra of protons formed via the mechanisms associated with the excitation and fragmentation of the projectile nucleus.

The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to separate the contributions of different mechanisms to the production of protons at different angles in 16Op reactions at a momentum of about 3.25 GeV/c per nucleon by analyzing the momentum spectra of protons in the laboratory system.
the shape of the proton momentum spectrum is a sensitive tool for probing the degree of excitaion of the fragmenting system and the relative contributions of different fragmentation mechanisms.
the shape of the proton momentum spectrum of the 16O+Au reaction is determined by both the degree of excita-tion of the fragmenting system and the reaction mechanism of the proton production.
